memorize

/MEM-uh-ryze/ - stress on MEM · verb

Hear It

What It Means

Memorize means to fix something in your memory exactly, so you can call it back word for word without looking.

Old helmsmen memorized all thirty-two points of the compass in order, boxing the whole rose from north to north before anyone trusted them at the wheel.

Example

For the citizenship interview, Guillermina memorized all one hundred civics answers — not roughly but to the comma, because the officer could open with any ten of them and would not repeat a question twice.

Memorize is the precise word because her preparation aimed at exact recall: the answers stored word for word, ready without notes. Study would only say she worked at the material, and review would say she went back over it; memorize names the finished state — the words are in her head, complete, on demand.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

retain: Retain is about keeping: information already learned stays put instead of fading. Memorize names the deliberate work at the front end — fixing the material exactly, word for word, so there is something to retain. You memorize the speech on Tuesday and hope to retain it by Friday.

rehearse: Rehearse means to run something through repeatedly to prepare — and you can rehearse with the script still in your hand. Memorize means the words themselves are stored, exact and complete, so the page can close. A cast rehearses for weeks; each actor must also memorize the part.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

forget: to let something slip out of memory

improvise: to produce on the spot, with nothing stored in advance

Where it sits · how deeply the words are fixed in mind

review → memorize → internalize

review vs. memorize: Review is weaker than memorize: reviewing passes back over the material to refresh it, while memorizing fixes it exactly, ready to repeat without looking.

internalize vs. memorize: Internalize goes deeper than memorize: memorized words can be recited on cue, but internalized ideas have soaked in so far they guide you without any conscious recall.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — memor-: mindful, remembering (Latin memor)

Suffix — -ize: to make, to cause to be

Put it together: Memor- (mindful) + -ize (to make) = 'to make oneself mindful of' — to set something into the mind on purpose. The same root keeps memory, memoir, and commemorate in one family; memorize is its workhorse, the deliberate act of moving words from the page into the head.

Use the root in a new word: commemorate: A single worn coin, struck in 1897, commemorates the lighthouse that once stood out on the point.

Word Choice

plain / study-hall practical

Memorize is the exact-storage verb: it promises the words themselves, retrievable without the page — lines, formulas, compass points. It says nothing about understanding; a student can memorize a proof without following it, or follow it cold and memorize nothing. In SAT passages about education, watch for exactly that contrast — memorization set against genuine grasp. Rehearse is the practicing and retain is the keeping; memorize is the act of getting it in, whole and word-perfect.
